To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the content of collagen and its soluble and insoluble fractions, glycoprotein and nucleic acid concentrations, and also lipid content in the lung tissue change in rats during postnatal ontogeny.
the collagen content in lungs increases with age, and that there is an increase in the amount of insoluble collagen in the lungs.
the content of soluble and insolube collagen fractions, as well as of RNA, hexose, hexuronic acid, tyrosine and sialic acid in rat lungs changes with age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the changes in the content of the main components of the connective tissue during ageing.
the changes in content of the main components of lung connective tissue and their relationship in the process of ageing.
the age-related changes in content of the main components of lung connective tissue, which are important in the maintenance of lung function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in ageing of rat lung connectives the processes of collagen synthesis, degradation and crosslinking are in a dynamic equilibrium, while the processes of synthesis and degradation of other connective tissue components are in a state of balance. the changes in the connective tissue of rat lungs in the process of ageing were determined by a series of factors.
ageing of lung connective tissue was characterized by the loss of collagen, its solubility, decrease in glycosamine glycane content and increase in phospholiptids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the changes in content of soluble collagen, hexosamines, DNA and phospholipids are characteristic for the ageing of lungs.

the changes in the content of connective tissue components in the course of ageing of the lungs are characterized by a gradual decrease of the amount of soluble collagen, RNA and DNA with a simultaneous increase in phospho- and sphingolipids.
the ageing process is characterized by a gradual decrease in the rate of biosynthetic reactions and by a gradual decrease of the rate of collagen turnover.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the content of soluble collagen is maximal in young animals and decreases with ageing.
the content of soluble collagen is maximal in juvenile animals, while that of insoluble collagen in old ones.
ageing is accompanied by the change of collagen content, which is reflected in the change of the ratio of its fractions.
